activities.anchor: Try to doubt your own existence
activities.caption: bet on what the cogito buys
activities.name: metaCogitoPredict

config.q: Descartes' foundation: what exactly does "I think, therefore I am" establish?
choices: That you exist as a thinking thing — nothing about your body or the chair
That the external world exists, since thinking needs objects
config.why: A tiny foundation, absolutely secure — which is why the next four centuries of philosophy are built on and around rebuilding outward from it.

activities.anchor: which splits into two great camps
activities.caption: file the monist camps
activities.name: metaMonismSort

config.prompt: Monism splits into two great camps — file each claim:

items.label: its hard case is consciousness: brain states and felt pain seem like different sorts of thing
brain states and experiences are perfectly correlated — that bit of the brain lights up when the toe hurts
some versions posit a single cosmic mind; others many minds and their experiences
the study of experience-as-had became the school called phenomenology

config.why: The argument between the camps is alive, unresolved, and arguably the deepest question in the subject — correlation is not identity.

activities.caption: pair each answer to the problem of universals
activities.name: metaUniversalsMatch

config.prompt: The oldest problem on the books — pair each answer with its claim:

pairs.right: universals live in a timeless realm of Forms — apples participate in Redness itself
no redness without red things — the properties live in the things
only particulars exist — "red" is a name, a resemblance, not a thing
numbers behave like realist universals — objective, necessary, shared — yet never appear in any experiment

config.why: "Is mathematics discovered or invented?" is the problem of universals wearing casual clothes.

config.root: Numbers behave like realist universals — objective, necessary, shared by all their instances — while never being found in any experiment.

choices.label: Yes — platonism: non-physical but real
choices.feedback: Then mathematics is discovered — but where, if not in space, time or any experiment?

choices.label: No — nominalism: an indispensable fiction
choices.feedback: Then mathematics is invented — yet its objectivity and necessity still need explaining.

plat.text: Benacerraf's dilemma waits down the road: if numbers exist outside space and time, how do we know them?

nom.text: If they do not exist, why is mathematics objectively true? Fifty years after Benacerraf, no consensus — the inventory stays open.

config.why: Ontology's hardest open case remains mathematics — and it matters, because the answer shapes what the world contains.

activities.anchor: persistence through change is genuinely unresolved
activities.caption: drag the divider — the ship that would not stay the same
activities.name: metaShipCompare

config.prompt: Drag the divider — the ship that would not stay the same:

before.label: The repaired ship
before.text: Spatiotemporal continuity: it stayed put in one continuous history — it is the same ship.

after.label: The reassembled planks
after.text: The old planks rebuilt as a second ship: psychological or biological continuity, four-dimensionalism ("stage-worms") and conventionalism each return a different verdict.

config.why: Still open — and the answer grounds personal identity, legal personhood and biological individuality.

activities.anchor: David Lewis's answer (1986) is the boldest
activities.caption: walk Lewis's trade — elegance against ontology
activities.name: metaLewisSteps

steps.note: "The coin could have landed tails" means: in some world, it did — possibilities are other concrete worlds, as real as ours, spatiotemporally isolated.
Modality becomes simple counting over worlds; modal logic gets clean truth-conditions.
An infinity of entire universes, most of them not containing you, existing for the sake of semantics.
Actualism: possibilities are ways THIS world could have been, built from abstract objects. Fictionalism: a useful make-believe.
